items.title: Frank Netto Interview, 1986-11-10
items.q: And, uh, Leon was just born.

ctx.x: joint. Huh? No, no, no, no, no, no, no, no, no. You didn't want to put them out of business then, but we worked up there until the night they raided it. I was on the bandstand when they raided it. They put a sticker on a little button and Getz, Tommy Getz was the guy that ran the place. He was the gambler. And he told me, he says, if you see me stick my finger in my ear like this, press this button over there to let them know in the gambling room that the police were here. So I told him, all right, it was laying…

Hebert was, uh, some dinner for Eddie Hebert, which I had the music for. And Kefaubber came down here, was when, Kefaubber was the one that put all of these guys out of business. Yeah. Yeah. And, uh, they had a special, uh, before the dinner, they had the VIP room, cocktails before the dinner. And I went over there and Eddie, who had autographed my album. And, uh, Leon was just born. This was in 1952, 51. And, uh, I got Mr. Kefaubber to, uh, uh, to, uh, autograph my program, too. He was the principal speaker. So,…

Yeah, but you're talking about several years after. Yeah, this is after. This is long before that. Well, because when, uh, Huey Long was a guard, it shut, uh, shut Tommy Gets down. Yeah, he shut him down. So, uh, then we left there. We stayed there a few weeks after that. And, uh, we let, uh, then we let, uh, Johnny Laporte go because, I don't think Johnny played well enough. Bill didn't like him and Eddie Miller didn't like, care for him that much either. So then we went out. Our next job was the Hunnis, was,…
